issues.title: Single underscore include guard used
issues.description: The rule requires header files to use include guards with double underscores at the start (e.g., __FILENAME_H), but the code uses a single underscore prefix instead (_REDIS_H)
issues.rule_name: Header Files Must Use Double-Underscore Include Guards

issues.title: Unsigned integer wraparound in AOF corruption size check
issues.description: The size comparison casts both operands to size_t (unsigned), which causes undefined behavior when valid_up_to exceeds sb.st_size. In this edge case, the subtraction sb.st_size - valid_up_to produces a negative value that wraps around to a very large unsigned integer, always exceeding aof_load_broken_max_size. This prevents automatic recovery even when the corruption is actually small, causing the server to fail to start when it should recover successfully.

issues.title: Incorrect early exit prevents loading incremental AOF after successful base recovery
issues.description: The error handling condition incorrectly treats AOF_BROKEN_RECOVERED as a failure state, causing the function to exit immediately after successfully recovering a corrupted base AOF file. When a base AOF is the last file and gets successfully recovered (ret == AOF_BROKEN_RECOVERED), the server should continue to load any incremental AOF files. However, this bug causes an early exit to cleanup, preventing incremental files from being loaded and potentially losing data. The correct behavior is to only exit on AOF_OPEN_ERR or AOF_FAILED, not on successful recovery.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #14058 - Add auto-repair options for broken AOF tail on startup
pr.author: unknown

structured_output.summary:
This PR adds two opt-in settings, aof-load-broken (default off) and aof-load-broken-max-size (default 4096 bytes). When an AOF load hits a format error (fmterr) and the bytes after the last applied command are under the limit, Redis truncates the file at valid_up_to and returns a new AOF_BROKEN_RECOVERED code. The loader treats that code like the existing AOF_TRUNCATED path, including requiring it to be the last file. The config plumbing, the default-off behavior, and the disabled path are sound.

The recovery itself is not safe enough to merge. I found three ways the truncation point can be wrong: it can keep an unfinished MULTI block, it can keep a command whose argument bytes were torn and garbled, and it can wipe an RDB preamble when valid_up_to was never set. Each one turns a crash-damaged tail into silent data loss or corruption on the next restart. The tests also don't exercise the recovery path as written: a Tcl rm glob is a no-op, and earlier runs have already truncated the fixtures, so several recovery cases would pass with the feature removed. The unrelated include-guard rename in server.h should be dropped.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The recovery path can lose acknowledged writes, can persist garbled commands, and can wipe an RDB preamble, and the tests don't prove the recovery works. The MULTI and preamble defects are concrete and follow directly from the code. They need fixing before this is safe even as an opt-in, though it is off by default.

architecture.overview:
At startup, loadDataFromDisk() in src/server.c calls loadAppendOnlyFiles(), which replays the base file and then each incremental file through loadSingleAppendOnlyFile() in src/aof.c. That function reads RESP commands one at a time, executes each on a fake client, and records valid_up_to after each successful command. Before this PR, any format error aborted the load with AOF_FAILED, which makes the server exit. The only existing self-repair was aof-load-truncated, which handles a short read at EOF by truncating to valid_up_to.

The PR adds aof-load-broken and aof-load-broken-max-size, wired through src/config.c and redis.conf. In the fmterr branch, when the option is on and the bytes after valid_up_to are under the limit, the file is truncated and the load returns AOF_BROKEN_RECOVERED. loadAppendOnlyFiles() then treats that code like AOF_TRUNCATED, failing the startup if the file is not the last one.
steps: Startup entry point: loadDataFromDisk() in src/server.c calls loadAppendOnlyFiles(server.aof_manifest) when AOF is enabled, and exits only on AOF_FAILED or AOF_OPEN_ERR.
Per-file replay: loadSingleAppendOnlyFile() in src/aof.c parses one RESP command at a time, runs it on a fake client, and updates valid_up_to after each command (line 1661).

New decision point: the fmterr label (src/aof.c around 1724-1756) now checks aof_load_broken. If the tail is under the limit, it truncates the file at valid_up_to and jumps to loaded_ok with AOF_BROKEN_RECOVERED.

Manifest-level gating: loadAppendOnlyFiles() in src/aof.c treats AOF_BROKEN_RECOVERED like AOF_TRUNCATED, so it is only acceptable on the last file. The truncation itself happens before that check runs.

Configuration: aof-load-broken (default no) and aof-load-broken-max-size (default 4096) are registered in src/config.c and documented in redis.conf. The PR also adds a new AOF_BROKEN_RECOVERED constant and two server fields in src/server.h.

diagrams.title: AOF startup load with the broken-tail recovery branch
diagrams.description: Startup replays AOF files; a format error either fails startup or, with the new option, truncates the tail and continues if the file is last.
diagrams.mermaid:
flowchart TD
  A["loadDataFromDisk (server.c)"] --> B["loadAppendOnlyFiles (aof.c)"]
  B --> C["loadSingleAppendOnlyFile per base or incr file"]
  C --> D{"fmterr: malformed command"}
  D -->|aof_load_broken off| E["AOF_FAILED: exit 1"]
  D -->|aof_load_broken on and tail under max size| F["truncate at valid_up_to, AOF_BROKEN_RECOVERED"]
  D -->|aof_load_broken on and tail too large| E
  F --> G{"last file?"}
  G -->|yes| H["startup continues"]
  G -->|no| E

findings.title: Recovery truncation keeps an unfinished MULTI block, so later writes are reverted on the next restart
findings.fixPrompt: In src/aof.c, in the fmterr branch of loadSingleAppendOnlyFile (around lines 1724-1734), the recovery truncates to valid_up_to. That value already includes commands queued inside an unfinished MULTI, so the file keeps a dangling transaction and the next restart reverts writes made after recovery. Before the truncate, if fakeClient->flags has CLIENT_MULTI set, use valid_before_multi as the cut point, the same way the EOF branch does at lines 1670-1674. Add a test: write MULTI, a SET, then a garbage tail; start with aof-load-broken yes; write a key; restart; assert the key survives.

findings.title: Argument terminators are not validated, so a torn command can run with garbled bytes and be kept
findings.fixPrompt: In src/aof.c, loadSingleAppendOnlyFile reads each bulk argument (around lines 1594-1622) and discards the two bytes after it without checking that they are CRLF. A torn write with zero-filled bytes can therefore run a garbled command, and because valid_up_to advances afterwards, aof-load-broken keeps that command in the file. Check that the two terminator bytes are CRLF, and jump to fmterr on mismatch, before the command is executed. Also update the Bad format test in tests/integration/aof.tcl (around lines 778-795) so it asserts that no key named foc exists after recovery.

findings.title: RDB preamble is wiped when the first AOF command after it is malformed, because valid_up_to is never set
findings.fixPrompt: In src/aof.c, loadSingleAppendOnlyFile never sets valid_up_to after the RDB preamble loads (around lines 1539-1553). The fmterr recovery (around lines 1724-1728) then truncates to 0 and wipes the preamble when the first AOF command after it is malformed. After the preamble loads successfully, set valid_up_to to ftello(fp), next to the existing last_progress_report_size assignment. This also fixes the same latent truncate-to-zero in the aof-load-truncated path around line 1694. Add a test: an RDB-preamble file under 4 KiB with a garbage tail, started with aof-load-broken yes; assert the preamble's keys survive a restart.

findings.title: Corrupted middle file is truncated on disk before the fatal not-last-file check
findings.body:
The truncation happens inside loadSingleAppendOnlyFile, before loadAppendOnlyFiles decides whether the file is the last one (aof.c lines 1836-1839 and 1870-1873). If a middle file is malformed, Redis truncates it on disk, logs AOF loaded anyway, then logs Fatal error: the truncated file is not the last file and exits. The on-disk file has been changed even though startup fails, and the first log line says the opposite of what happened. The new test at tests/integration/aof.tcl lines 715-721 encodes that misleading message.

::diff{file="src/aof.c" lines="1727-1741"}
findings.fixPrompt: In src/aof.c, the fmterr recovery in loadSingleAppendOnlyFile (around lines 1724-1745) truncates the file before loadAppendOnlyFiles knows whether this file is the last one. A malformed middle file is therefore modified on disk and then the server refuses to start, while logging that the AOF was loaded anyway. Move the truncation out of loadSingleAppendOnlyFile. Return a recoverable status with the cut offset, and let loadAppendOnlyFiles truncate only after the last_file check passes. Update the log message so it matches what happened, and update the test at tests/integration/aof.tcl lines 715-721 to match.

findings.title: Truncation removes every byte after the first bad command, including valid later writes
findings.fixPrompt: The aof-load-broken recovery in src/aof.c (fmterr branch, around lines 1724-1728) truncates everything from valid_up_to to end of file, so a corrupt byte in the middle of the file also deletes valid commands that follow it, up to aof-load-broken-max-size bytes. Either (a) make the redis.conf text in redis.conf lines 1532-1541 say explicitly that all data after the first bad command is discarded, or (b) additionally require that no further well-formed RESP command can be parsed after the bad byte before recovering. Pick one and make the code and docs agree.

findings.title: rm -f glob in the test is a no-op, so the base-as-last-file case never exercises recovery
findings.body:
exec rm -f $aof_dirpath/appendonly.aof.* does not glob-expand, because Tcl exec passes the literal asterisk to rm. I checked with tclsh: the files remain. So the incremental file is never removed, and the base file still holds the set param ok content that the previous fatal run already truncated to, with no corruption left. The test reports that the base file recovers, but it passes even if the recovery code is removed.

::diff{file="tests/integration/aof.tcl" lines="724-731"}
findings.fixPrompt: In tests/integration/aof.tcl (around lines 724-731), the exec rm -f with a * glob is a no-op because Tcl exec does not glob-expand. Replace it with foreach over glob -nocomplain on the incremental files, and file delete each one. Before starting the server, rewrite the base file with create_aof so that it contains a corrupt tail, since the earlier fatal run already truncated it. Then the param equals ok assertion actually checks that recovery happened.

findings.title: Swap test passes without any corruption, because the earlier run already truncated the file
findings.body:
The Intermediate AOF is broken case runs with aof-load-broken yes. The middle file is non-last, so the recovery truncates it to set fo mid, and the server then exits. After the swap, the file at .2 is that already-truncated file, so the Corrupted last AOF file test starts from clean data. Removing the recovery code entirely still passes this test. It never checks that the last-file recovery works.

::code{file="tests/integration/aof.tcl" lines="832-837"}
findings.fixPrompt: In tests/integration/aof.tcl, the Corrupted last AOF file test (around lines 825-837) runs after the Intermediate AOF is broken case, which already truncated the middle file to remove its CORRUPTION tail. After the swap, the file at the last position holds clean data, so the test checks nothing about recovery. Re-create the last file with a corrupt tail (for example, append a CORRUPTION line) immediately before starting the server, so the test depends only on its own fixture.

findings.title: wait_for_log_messages matches any pattern, so the Log should mention test can pass on one line alone
findings.body:
tests/support/util.tcl (lines 212-216) returns as soon as any one pattern matches a line. The test at lines 715-721 lists two patterns, but the loaded-anyway line by itself is enough to pass. The Fatal error line the test is named for is never checked. Split the check into two calls, or wait for the fatal line only.

::diff{file="tests/integration/aof.tcl" lines="715-721"}
findings.fixPrompt: In tests/integration/aof.tcl, the test Log should mention truncated file is not last (around lines 715-721) passes wait_for_log_messages two patterns. That helper returns on the first pattern that matches (tests/support/util.tcl lines 212-216), so the misleading loaded anyway line is enough to pass. Replace it with two separate wait_for_log_messages calls, one for the Fatal error line and one for the loaded-anyway line, so both must be present.

findings.title: New AOF_BROKEN_RECOVERED code is not wired into the success bookkeeping
findings.body:
Three places treat AOF_TRUNCATED as success but not AOF_BROKEN_RECOVERED.

First, when the recovered file is the only base file, loadAppendOnlyFiles jumps to cleanup at line 1841-1842. That skips the server.aof_current_size and aof_rewrite_base_size assignments (lines 1881-1891) that the AOF_TRUNCATED path gets. Auto-rewrite and INFO then see zero sizes until the next write or rewrite.

Second, stopLoading(ret == AOF_OK || ret == AOF_TRUNCATED) at line 1894 reports LOADING_FAILED to modules for a startup that succeeded.

Third, the function header comment (lines 1477-1482) still lists only AOF_OK and AOF_TRUNCATED as success codes.

::diff{file="src/aof.c" lines="1841-1842"}
findings.fixPrompt: In src/aof.c, AOF_BROKEN_RECOVERED is handled inconsistently with AOF_TRUNCATED. The base-only goto cleanup at line 1841-1842 skips the server.aof_current_size and aof_rewrite_base_size bookkeeping at lines 1881-1891. The stopLoading call at line 1894 reports failure for a successful recovery. The header comment at lines 1477-1482 omits AOF_BROKEN_RECOVERED. Treat AOF_BROKEN_RECOVERED as success alongside AOF_TRUNCATED in the stopLoading check and in the base-file path, and update the header comment.

findings.title: Unrelated include-guard rename in server.h should be dropped
findings.body:
The PR changes the include guard from __REDIS_H to _REDIS_H. Nothing in the feature needs it. Both names are reserved identifiers in C, since they start with an underscore followed by a capital letter, so the change doesn't fix anything. It only adds noise to a feature PR. Revert it, or split it into its own change.

::diff{file="src/server.h" lines="15-16"}
findings.fixPrompt: In src/server.h lines 15-16, the include guard was renamed from __REDIS_H to _REDIS_H, which is unrelated to the AOF change. Revert that rename so the guard matches the original, or move it into a separate cleanup change. Note that both names begin with an underscore followed by a capital letter, so neither is a safe identifier.

findings.title: Test coverage is missing for the new failure modes, and some test names are misleading
findings.body:
The new tests don't cover the cases most likely to break recovery. Missing: an open MULTI at the malformed point, a zero-filled tail, a file that is only an RDB preamble plus garbage, and a malformed command followed by valid commands. The tests named Short read: Server should start if aof-load-broken is yes (line 748) and Short read + command (line 766) cover format errors, not short reads, so the names will mislead anyone reading failures.

::code{file="tests/integration/aof.tcl" lines="748-766"}
findings.fixPrompt: In tests/integration/aof.tcl, add tests for: (1) a malformed tail inside an open MULTI, checking that writes made after recovery survive a second restart; (2) a zero-filled tail; (3) an RDB-preamble base file followed by a garbage tail, checking that the preamble's keys survive; (4) a malformed command followed by valid commands, to pin down the documented truncation behavior. Also rename the tests at lines 748 and 766 so they say format error rather than short read.

findings.title: Opt-in default and config defaults line up across redis.conf, config.c, and server.h
findings.body: aof-load-broken defaults to off in redis.conf (line 1548), and createBoolConfig in src/config.c (line 3093) uses default 0. aof-load-broken-max-size defaults to 4096 in redis.conf (line 1549) and in the createOffTConfig default in src/config.c (line 3258). Both are MODIFIABLE, and the disabled path keeps the original fatal message. For a feature that can silently drop data, defaulting to off is the right call.

findings.title: Recovery reuses the existing truncate and seek sequence
findings.body: The fmterr recovery mirrors the existing aof-load-truncated code: it truncates, reseats aof_fd with lseek to SEEK_END, and only then reports success. The new return code is gated on last_file in the same way AOF_TRUNCATED is. Reviewers familiar with the uxeof branch will recognize the pattern, though the duplicated truncation block could be pulled into a helper.
